reason:
The operative contract here is problem.txt (no test.py/get_inputs exist): out must be one of the two neighbouring multiples of STEP=0.05 with P(upper)=(x-lower)/STEP so that E[out]==x, randomness from tl.rand seeded by the caller, over 1-D power-of-two-length single-block inputs. The kernel (kernel.py:12-17) is a literal transcription of that formula, and each of the three stated requirements is backed by runtime evidence on in-domain inputs.

c2 (grid/neighbour violation from the non-representability of 0.05) is rebutted by t10: for x = k*0.05, k in -64..63, and x +/- 1 ulp, over 200 seeds per family, max off-grid deviation was exactly 0.0 and no element ever moved a full STEP away from an exact grid point, even though 7.03% of exact multiples do hit the floor(x/STEP)*STEP != x hazard on the host. c3 (RNG degeneracy across offsets) is rebutted by t11: constant input with p_up=0.5, N=4096, 64 seeds gave per-seed upper-fractions 0.4834-0.5261 (max |z| 3.34), longest run 17 vs the ~12 expected for iid bits, lag-1 autocorrelation 0.0015, 64 distinct patterns, cross-seed agreement 0.524 (chance), and identical output for a repeated seed (counter-based determinism intact).

c1 is the one claim still formally logged as inconclusive, because its first probe (t9) used a bitwise-equality membership test against a host fp32 reference; that metric was self-refuting — the frequency deficit (-0.1408) matched the non-member fraction (0.1407) almost exactly, i.e. an artifact of last-bit differences, not a Bernoulli bias. I am not setting the claim aside on rhetoric: the follow-up tool event t15 re-ran it with a double-precision nearest-neighbour classifier over 8000 seeds on 1024 mixed structured-and-random in-domain values, and found per-element upper-frequency consistent with p_true (max |z| = 4.22 over 1024 elements, frac |z|>5 = 0.0, mean z = -0.048, std z = 1.03 — exactly the profile of correct independent Bernoulli draws), grand mean(out)-x = -7.48e-06 at z = -1.07 against its own sampling sigma, outside_neighbour_count = 0, and max off-grid distance 2.86e-07 (~0.6 fp32 ulp at |x|=5, 5.7e-6 of STEP). That residual sub-ulp deviation is ordinary fp32 representation error in reconstructing multiples of a non-representable 0.05, which the contract's fp32 tensor semantics account for; it is not a deviation from a behaviour the contract requires. The Skeptic reviewed t15 and recorded no new claims.

Generalization limits I am explicitly not treating as defects, since problem.txt restricts the domain to 1-D power-of-two-length single-block tensors: non-power-of-two or multi-block N, fp16/bf16 dtypes, non-contiguous or CPU tensors, and |x| large enough that x/STEP loses integer resolution remain untested.
